'''John Latham''' (21 July 1937 – 27 April 2021) was a British physicist and professor emeritus at the [[University of Manchester]], known for his work on [[atmospheric electricity]] and, later in his career, [[climate engineering]]. He was also an accomplished poet.

== Biography ==
Latham obtained a PhD on thunderstorm electrification from [[Imperial College London]], where he was supervised by [[John Mason (meteorologist)|John Mason]]. In 1961, he moved to [[Umist]], now part of [[Manchester University]], to take up a lectureship and founded the Atmospheric Physics research group.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Our History (Centre for Atmospheric Science – The University of Manchester)|url=http://www.cas.manchester.ac.uk/history/|access-date=2021-05-07|website=www.cas.manchester.ac.uk}}</ref> In 1988, he was hired as a senior research associate in ESSL/MMM<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.ucar.edu/492/ncar-scientist-namesake-new-british-lab|title = NCAR scientist is namesake of new British lab &#124; NCAR & UCAR News}}</ref> at the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]] (NCAR) in [[Colorado]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Carcanet Press – John Latham|url=https://www.carcanet.co.uk/cgi-bin/indexer?owner_id=405|access-date=2021-05-07|website=www.carcanet.co.uk}}</ref>

==Scientific achievements==
Latham is best known for his work on thunderstorm electrification<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Illingworth|first1=A. J.|last2=Latham|first2=J.|date=April 1977|title=Calculations of electric field growth, field structure and charge distributions in thunderstorms|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1002/qj.49710343606|journal=Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society|volume=103|issue=436|pages=281–295|doi=10.1002/qj.49710343606|issn=0035-9009|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[marine cloud brightening]],<ref>Latham, John (2002). "Amelioration of Global Warming by Controlled Enhancement of the Albedo and Longevity of Low-Level Maritime Clouds". Atmos. Sci. Letters. {{doi|10.1006/Asle.2002.0048}}</ref> a form of [[geoengineering]] which relies on [[seawater]] sprayed from ships. In collaboration with [[Stephen Salter]] he developed a scheme involving [[Flettner vessels]]. One of his major contributions to cloud formation theory came in 1979, with an emphasis on droplet growth and microphysics as modelled in warm clouds, namely those clouds that comprise water vapour and the microscopic droplets that begin to condense from it, rather than ice. A key problem in cloud physics was how to explain the rapid formation of droplets (something none of the models at that time were able to explain). Latham's hypothesis of “inhomogeneous mixing” involved discrete segments of dry air being transported into the clouds: these drier segments caused the complete evaporation of adjacent droplets, while droplets further away remained immune from the process; the fact that the cloud thereby contains fewer droplets explains why competition for the available water vapour in the cloud is reduced, allowing the largest drops to increase in size much faster than expected.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2021/may/30/john-latham-obituay|title = John Latham obituary: Climate physicist and expert on thunderstorm electrification who was also a published poet|access-date=18 November 2023|website=www.theguardian.com}}</ref>

In his academic career, he supervised over twenty-five doctoral students,<ref name=":0" /> the first of whom was David Stow.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=728612|title = Physics Tree - David Stow}}</ref><ref name="University of Manchester - science and literary biography and obituary">{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/professor-john-latham-1937-2021/| title = doctoral students (Professor John Latham, 1937-2021) and Literary biography - The University of Manchester) |access-date=2 December 2023 }}</ref>

==Literary achievements==
Latham was also a talented prose writer, playwright and prize-winning poet.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The UK Poetry Society |work=John Latham biography (the Poetry Society website) |access-date=2 December 2023 |url=https://poems.poetrysociety.org.uk/poets/john-latham/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119203711/https://poems.poetrysociety.org.uk/poets/john-latham/ |archive-date=19 January 2022 |url-status=live }}</ref> He won first prize in over twenty poetry competitions, with the title poem for one of his later collections (entitled 'From Professor Murasaki’s Notebooks on the Effects of Lightning on the Human Body') gaining second prize in the UK’s 2006 National Poetry Competition.<ref>{{Cite web |title=National Poetry competition |work=administered through the Poetry Society (United Kingdom) |access-date=2 December 2023 |url=https://poetrysociety.org.uk/poems/from-professor-nobu-kitagawas-notebooks-on-effects-of-lightning-on-the-human-body-tr-from-the-japanese-by-n-kitagawa/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210014109/https://poetrysociety.org.uk/poems/from-professor-nobu-kitagawas-notebooks-on-effects-of-lightning-on-the-human-body-tr-from-the-japanese-by-n-kitagawa/ |archive-date=10 February 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> He published six full collections of poetry in all<ref name="Guardian_2021">{{Cite web |title=John Latham obituary |author=Alan Gadian |work=the Guardian |date=30 May 2021 |access-date=3 June 2021 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/science/2021/may/30/john-latham-obituay}}</ref> and broadcast a number of radio plays on BBC Radio 4.<ref>{{Cite web|title=John Latham – Comma Press|url=https://commapress.co.uk/authors/john-latham/|access-date=2021-05-07|website=commapress.co.uk}}</ref>

Latham's poetry is characterised by the kind of close observation typical of a scientist, combined with a natural ability to generate "a strikingly original angle of vision” whose metaphors "hang around in the mind long after you’ve read them”.<ref name="Colorado Poets Center">{{Cite web |title=Colorado Poets Center: John Latham - Critical Commentary, Some Reviews of UK Poetry Collections |access-date=2 December 2023 |url=https://coloradopoetscenter.org/poets/latham_john/commentary.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231118140501/https://coloradopoetscenter.org/poets/latham_john/commentary.html/ |archive-date=18 November 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref> His poems received positive reviews from poets [[Ian McMillan (poet)|Ian McMillan]], [[Peter Porter (poet)|Peter Porter]] and [[John Greening]], and he was published and/or reviewed in many literary outlets (including the [[The Observer|Observer]] and [[Poetry Review]]). His later work focused more intently on the themes of ageing and memory, a significant feature of his writing as dementia took hold, complicating the latter years of his life.<ref name="University of Manchester - science and literary biography and obituary" />
